comment: The three CLIs the copilot can be, and what they offer before they are asked. Shared because both processes need it: electron/ai.js decides what it will spawn, src/models.js decides what the dropdown shows, and two copies of that is how the two disagree. `offerByDefault` is false for opencode alone — its catalogue is an account property running to several hundred entries, which is what the Models-offered setting exists to keep out of the list. The Claude labels and context figures below are the fallback: at catalogue time ai.js asks the CLI itself (`claude models list`) and writes its labels over these, because an id like `opus` is an alias that follows the newest model of that name — the stale label used to have to be moved by hand on every Anthropic release. The fallback still decides which aliases are offered and which effort levels each takes, neither of which the lineup table publishes. `grants` is what each CLI can actually do in each of the two modes, in the user's words: Claude takes a tool allowlist and so gets no shell at all, while Codex and opencode have no per-tool switch and are fenced only by a sandbox — one toggle, three blast radii, and the panel says which one it is handing over.

grants.write: read, edit and create notes, and run shell commands inside the vault
read, edit and create notes, run shell commands inside the vault, and fetch web pages
